'''Jörg Dräger''' (born 1 January 1968 in [[Darmstadt]]) is a German [[physicist]], politician and manager who has been the executive director of the board of trustees of Kühne Foundation since 2022.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Zukunft entscheidet sich im Klassenzimmer|date=29 August 2011|language=de|author=Bernhard Hänel|newspaper=Neue Westfälische}}</ref><ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Board of Trustees {{!}} Kühne Foundation |url=https://www.kuehne-stiftung.org/foundation/foundation-council |access-date=2026-05-22 |website=www.kuehne-stiftung.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Dr. Jörg Dräger wird Geschäftsführender Stiftungsrat |url=http://www.kuehne-stiftung.org/de/media/archiv/dr-joerg-draeger-to-become-executive-director-of-the-board-of-trustees |access-date=2026-05-22 |website=www.kuehne-stiftung.org |language=de-DE}}</ref>

From 2001 to 2008 he was a senator in the [[Government of Hamburg|Hamburg state government]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Wege aus der Bildungskrise|date=29 August 2011|language=de|author=Elisabeth Jessen|newspaper=Hamburger Abendblatt}}</ref> From 2008 to 2021 he has been a member of the [[Bertelsmann Stiftung]] Executive Board where he was responsible for the areas of education, integration and digitalisation.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Hamburgs Wissenschaftssenator wechselt zu Bertelsmann|date=5 March 2008|language=de|newspaper=Der Tagesspiegel}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.manager-magazin.de/unternehmen/karriere/a-539338.html|title=Bertelsmann: Dräger geht zur Stiftung|date=4 March 2008|website=Manager Magazin|language=de|access-date=30 June 2017}}</ref> Dräger is considered a leading education expert<ref>{{Cite news|title=Das wird ein Angriff auf die Eliten|date=27 September 2015|language=de|author=Jörn Lauterbach|newspaper=[[Welt am Sonntag]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.waz.de/mediacampus/fuer-lehrer/unterrichtshilfen/das-abitur-wird-zum-normalfall-id210015443.html|title=Bildungsexperte Dräger: Das Abitur wird zum Normalfall|date=22 March 2017|website=Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung|language=de|access-date=30 June 2017}}</ref> and is the author of numerous books on education policy,<ref>{{Cite news|title=Wieder ein Schulbuch: Spät, aber wichtig|date=31 August 2011|language=de|author=Michael Okrob|newspaper=Die Tageszeitung}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Debatte über das Lernen der Zukunft|date=1 April 2016|language=de|newspaper=[[Die Welt]]}}</ref> including the impacts of digitization.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.zeit.de/2015/39/digitalisierung-bildung-internet-computer-lehrplan/komplettansicht|title=Digitalisierung: Humboldt gegen Orwell|date=8 October 2015|website=[[Die Zeit]]|language=de|access-date=5 July 2017|author=Jörg Dräger, Ralph Müller-Eiselt}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Dräger completed his secondary education ([[Abitur]]) in 1987 at the Christianeum in Hamburg before doing community service in lieu of military service ([[Zivildienst]]).<ref>{{Cite news|title=Ich brauche kein Lob|date=31 August 2004|language=de|author=Renate Pinzke|newspaper=Hamburger Morgenpost}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.munzinger.de/document/00000023909|title=Jörg Dräger|date=9 September 2008|website=Internationales Biographisches Archiv|publisher=Munzinger|language=de|access-date=30 June 2017}}</ref> He then attended the [[University of Hamburg]], studying physics with a minor in business.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|title=Reformer mit kühlem Kopf|date=21 August 2005|language=de|author=Florian Hanauer|newspaper=Welt am Sonntag}}</ref> After receiving his undergraduate degree ([[Vordiplom]]) he transferred to [[Cornell University]] in [[Ithaca, New York|Ithaca]], New York, where he was awarded a Master of Science in [[theoretical physics]] in 1993.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|title=Bildung ist die Basis|date=2 July 2008|language=de|newspaper=Neue Westfälische}}</ref> Three years later he received a PhD for his work in the area of mathematical crystallography.<ref name=":0" /> While studying and completing his doctorate he worked as a research assistant.<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
In 1996, he joined [[Roland Berger (company)|Roland Berger Strategy Consultants]] in Frankfurt am Main as a corporate consultant.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Hochschulen, Studienreform und Arbeitsmärkte: Voraussetzungen erfolgreicher Beschäftigungs- und Hochschulpolitik|year=2003|publisher=W. Bertelsmann Verlag|isbn=3-7639-3168-6|location=Bielefeld|page=286|editor=Norbert Bensel}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Unis: Wer baut aus, wer baut ab?|date=21 March 2002|language=de|author=Peter Meyer, Christoph Rind|newspaper=Hamburger Abendblatt}}</ref> He then returned to Hamburg in 1999 to lead the newly established [[Northern Institute of Technology Management|Northern Institute of Technology]] as its CEO.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.welt.de/print-wams/article118176/Der-Laptop-Senator.html|title=Der Laptop-Senator|date=26 January 2003|website=Welt am Sonntag|language=de|access-date=30 June 2017|author=Nicola Sieverling}}</ref> The institute is one of the first public-private partnerships in the area of German higher education and is known for its interdisciplinary approach.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Ausruhen gibt es hier nicht|date=15 August 1999|language=de|author=Wolfgang Ehemann|newspaper=Welt am Sonntag}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Die Besten der Besten studieren jetzt in Harburg|date=17 August 1999|language=de|author=Deborah Knür|newspaper=Die Welt}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Northern Institute of Technology: Wirtschaft zieht voll mit|date=17 December 1999|language=de|newspaper=Hamburger Abendblatt}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.zeit.de/2000/36/Jenseits_der_Technik/komplettansicht|title=Jenseits der Technik|date=31 August 2000|website=Die Zeit|language=de|access-date=30 June 2017|author=Petra Kipphoff}}</ref>

=== Public Office ===
In 2001, Dräger was appointed senator of science and research in Hamburg's state government led by [[Ole von Beust]], a position he held as a political independent.<ref>{{Cite news|title=An die Arbeit, Herr Senator!|date=20 November 2001|language=de|author=Christoph Rind|newspaper=Hamburger Abendblatt}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.zeit.de/2004/44/C-Dr_9ager/komplettansicht|title=Der Quereinsteiger|date=21 October 2004|access-date=30 June 2017|language=de|author=Arnfrid Schenk|website=Die Zeit}}</ref> He called for the introduction of tuition fees and more competition among higher education institutions to secure the institutions' long-term funding.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Gebühren und mehr Wettbewerb|date=13 November 2001|language=de|author=Christoph Rind|newspaper=Hamburger Abendblatt}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Drägers Uni-Modell|date=24 October 2001|language=de|author=Kaija Kutter|newspaper=Die Tageszeitung}}</ref> These recommendations were greeted with criticism, especially by student representatives.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Unerwünschter Auftritt|date=15 November 2001|edition=Hamburg|language=de|author=Kaija Kutter|newspaper=Die Tageszeitung}}</ref>

After early elections in 2004, Dräger was appointed senator of science and health in the second von Beust government.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|title=Das sind Oles neue Senatoren|date=16 March 2004|language=de|newspaper=Hamburger Morgenpost}}</ref> Continuing to advocate for reform, he succeeded in introducing [[Tuition payments|tuition fees]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=An der Problemlage hat sich nichts geändert|date=25 March 2004|language=de|author=Ira von Mellenthin|newspaper=Die Welt}}</ref> His goal was a fundamental reform of Hamburg's university system.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.zeit.de/2003/07/B-Uni_Kasten/komplettansicht|title=Blaupause für deutsche Universitäten|date=6 February 2003|access-date=30 June 2017|language=de|author=Martin Spiewak|website=Die Zeit}}</ref> He promoted the establishment of new institutions and the consolidation of existing ones as a way of modernizing Hamburg's higher education structures and making them more flexible.<ref name=":0" /> In retrospect these measures have proven controversial:<ref>{{Cite news|title=Umkrempeln um jeden Preis|date=16 January 2006|language=de|newspaper=Parlament}}</ref> While supporters praised his expertise and determination, critics opposed cutbacks made in the humanities, among other changes.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.zeit.de/2005/13/P-Dr_8ager/komplettansicht|title=Tortenschlacht um den Überzeugungstäter|date=23 March 2005|access-date=30 June 2017|language=de|author=Martin Spiewak|website=Die Zeit}}</ref> In 2008, Dräger placed last in the ranking of ministers published by the German Association of University Professors and Lecturers; one year later he again placed sixth.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.spiegel.de/lebenundlernen/uni/minister-ranking-die-professoren-keilen-aus-a-536868.html|title=Die Professoren keilen aus|date=21 February 2008|website=[[Spiegel Online]]|language=de|access-date=30 June 2017|author=Jochen Leffers}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.spiegel.de/lebenundlernen/uni/minister-ranking-ein-bisschen-spass-muss-sein-a-604116.html|title=Ein bisschen Spaß muss sein|date=28 January 2009|website=Spiegel Online|language=de|access-date=30 June 2017|author=Jochen Leffers}}</ref>

In 2006, he turned over his responsibilities in the area of health to Senator [[Birgit Schnieber-Jastram]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Neue Senatorin für Gesundheit in Hamburg|date=24 March 2006|language=de|newspaper=Ärzte Zeitung}}</ref> Following elections in 2008 he announced that he would not serve another term.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.spiegel.de/lebenundlernen/uni/hamburgs-wissenschaftssenator-joerg-draeger-verlaesst-die-politik-a-539257.html|title=Jörg Dräger verlässt die Politik|date=4 March 2008|website=Spiegel Online|language=de|access-date=30 June 2017}}</ref> His announcement was met with regret by a number of public figures, including former Hamburg Mayor [[Klaus von Dohnányi|Klaus von Dohnanyi]], who wrote in a commentary in the [[Hamburger Abendblatt]] newspaper that the city had lost presumably its "most effective science senator since 1945."<ref>{{Cite news|title=Wegweisende Entscheidungen|date=5 March 2008|language=de|newspaper=Hamburger Abendblatt}}</ref> Other members of the media, conversely, were relieved that the "bulldozer in the three-piece suit" ([[Die Tageszeitung|taz]]) was leaving politics.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Bulldozer im Dreiteiler: Jörg Dräger, Wissenschaftsenator auf Abruf|date=5 March 2008|language=de|newspaper=Die Tageszeitung}}</ref>

=== Bertelsmann Stiftung ===
From 2008 until the end of 2021, Dräger was a member of the [[Bertelsmann Stiftung]] Executive Board, where he was responsible for education, integration and digitalisation.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Senator Dräger wechselt zu Bertelsmann|date=5 March 2008|edition=Hamburg|language=de|author=Insa Gall|newspaper=Die Welt}}</ref><ref name=":1"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=Jörg Dräger verlässt die Bertelsmann Stiftung Ende 2021 - WELT |url=https://www.welt.de/regionales/nrw/article232204543/Joerg-Draeger-verlaesst-die-Bertelsmann-Stiftung-Ende-2021.html |access-date=2026-05-22 |website=DIE WELT |language=de}}</ref> In addition, he joined Frank Ziegele as a co-executive director of the nonprofit CHE [[Centre for Higher Education]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Der stolze Schlachter der heiligen Kühe|date=21 June 2008|language=de|author=Wolf Schmidt|newspaper=Die Tageszeitung}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Ein radikaler Reformer|date=23 June 2008|language=de|newspaper=Der Tagesspiegel}}</ref> In both positions Dräger has advocated for a number of reforms, including more autonomous colleges and universities.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Rankings ausbauen, Autonomie stärken|date=1 April 2008|language=de|author=Dorothee Fricke|newspaper=Junge Karriere}}</ref> He has called for providing schools in troubled neighborhoods with better equipment and resources, and ensuring that educational systems in rural areas adapt to reflect demographic change.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Ein Sofortprogramm für Brennpunktschulen ist überfällig!|date=8 December 2010|language=de|author=Jeannette Goddar|newspaper=[[Frankfurter Rundschau]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Investieren statt reparieren|date=20 February 2013|language=de|newspaper=Westfalen-Blatt}}</ref> He is in favor of [[all-day school]]s and views digital media as a helpful tool for improving education.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Ganztagsschule wird Normalität|date=30 January 2014|language=de|author=Michael Nichau|newspaper=Westfalen-Blatt}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Digitale Medien sind Hilfsmittel|date=22 June 2017|language=de|newspaper=Neue Westfälische (Zeitung für das Lübbecker Land)}}</ref>

Dräger was the deputy chair of the Board of Trustees of the Expert Council of the German Foundations on Integration and Migration.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kuratorium |url=https://www.svr-migration.de/sachverstaendigenrat/wir-ueber-uns/kuratorium/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200129125152/https://www.svr-migration.de/sachverstaendigenrat/wir-ueber-uns/kuratorium/ |archive-date=2020-01-29 |access-date=2026-05-22 |website=www.svr-migration.de |language=de-DE}}</ref> He has called for increased immigration from non-EU countries to ensure Germany does not lose out in the international competition for skilled workers.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Willkommen im Kanzleramt|date=29 May 2013|language=de|author=Daniel Bax|newspaper=Die Tageszeitung}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Ausländer rein!|date=1 September 2014|language=de|newspaper=Handelsblatt|author=Barbara Gillmann}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tagesspiegel.de/meinung/gastbeitrag-punkte-fuer-deutschland/6357064.html|title=Punkte für Deutschland|date=22 March 2012|website=Der Tagesspiegel|language=de|access-date=4 July 2017|author=Jörg Dräger}}</ref>

Dräger advises young entrepreneurs at the nonprofit Founders Foundation and teaches public management at the [[Hertie School of Governance]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Bertelsmann gibt Millionen für Firmengründer in OWL|date=17 February 2016|language=de|author=Martin Krause|newspaper=Neue Westfälische}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hertie-school.org/en/research/faculty-and-researchers/profile/person/draeger/|title=Jörg Dräger|publisher=Hertie School of Governance|language=de|access-date=30 June 2017|archive-date=1 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170801161435/https://www.hertie-school.org/en/research/faculty-and-researchers/profile/person/draeger/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Other activities==
* [[Jacobs University Bremen]], Member of the Board of Governors (since 2018)<ref>[https://www.jacobs-university.de/governance Governance] [[Jacobs University Bremen]].</ref>

==Personal life==
Dräger is married and has two children.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Dräger-Nachwuchs|date=9 June 2005|language=de|newspaper=Hamburger Abendblatt}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Guter Unterricht nimmt alle mit|date=20 January 2012|language=de|author=Bernd Eyermann|newspaper=Bonner General-Anzeiger}}</ref>
